May you give me a run-down on how it works?
It's virtualization software that gives VMs direct access to the hardware, something most virtualizers don't do. This was used by Linus Tech Tips for his 2-in1 and 7-in1 gaming machines.

Instead of running games on Wine directly, use PlayOnLinux instead. Even if you manage to run something via Wine, it might break with next Wine update – PlayOnLinux uses different versions of Wine for each app, which was proven to run the best in certain version. Just install POL and you'll see a list of supported software (not just games), which will download and install all the dependencies the soft needs + configuration. It's superior to Wine without so much troubleshooting and endless googling.

Of course the best is to play native games (with Steam having about 1/4 of all it's inventory available for Linux, if I'm not mistaken). I prefer this, as you also support the devs and make your "Linux voice" heard, as the devs can see which OSes are their gamers using. So you're promoting Linux gaming as well, which is always nice.
